decisions.summary: Every rule of the root CLAUDE.md is put to each of the twelve contracts, one rule and one agent at a time, no class of rule settled in advance; research.md holds a row per rule and a column per agent (stated / moved / does not bear).
decisions.why: FR-001's own method and record; unchanged by the wording correction and by both amendments.

decisions.summary: Both nested CLAUDE.md files are read for every check that works under either tree, by a behavioral criterion rather than a fixed roster; the table says per agent which tree it reads.
decisions.why: FR-001 asks the same reading of the two nested files for the checks that work there. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: A moved rule is written once, short, in the contract's own voice, in the section that already covers its subject or under a House rules heading.
decisions.why: FR-001 asks for the contract's own voice and no longer than the check needs. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: omitClaudeMd: true on its own line in each frontmatter, after effort:, with a parenthetical that P10 takes it off spec-fidelity.md again, 'approved by the GM on the session's recommendation (2026-09-20)'.
decisions.why: FR-002 as FR-013 now reads it. The parenthetical is the corrected wording and it is accurate against request.md's third block: the session put 'I can keep the field on or take it off for this one agent ... I recommend taking it off' and the GM answered 'go with your recommendations to all three'. It no longer claims a ruling the GM did not make. Verified in the tree: spec-fidelity.md is the only agent file without the field; the other eleven carry it after effort:.

decisions.summary: measure/dispatch_seeded.sh: a headless session in the case's worktree dispatches the agent once with the recorded prompt; the subagent's transcript gives reply, turns, usage and whether the prompt was verbatim; a non-verbatim run is discarded and re-run; control and candidate trees differ only in the field; scoring against the control first and the recorded findings second.
decisions.why: FR-003's setting, method and rule. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: FR-006's two legs are dispatched from /diagram, where the memory index actually loads, with the agent defined inline from entry-drift's real frontmatter and contract body; nothing written under the mirror; the worktree legs' no-index limit stated.
decisions.why: FR-006 asks for one real defined agent measured before and after. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Root CLAUDE.md's review-subagents bullet gains a sentence; docs/efficiency-tooling.md's feature-255 row gains the outcome; docs/review-ledger.md untouched.
decisions.why: FR-006 names those documents and no other, and forbids touching the review ledger. Unchanged.

decisions.summary: Amendment 1 edits two guard files - the skill's tests/test_agent_models.py (P6) and the skill Makefile (P8) - each with GUARD_EDIT_OK and a reason, where the first landing edited none; Amendment 2 edits the same test module again under the same line.
decisions.why: FR-007 names that test module and FR-009 asks for a make target; the escape is the repository's own route for an edit the spec demands. The authority named on this line - 'the GM's word of 2026-09-20' - is real: request.md's second block says 'I do indeed want the guard enforced by a test' and 'Please fix anything left unfixed'.

decisions.summary: The Route line stays DIRECT although the amendments' delta reaches the skill Makefile, the tier test and scripts/.
decisions.why: The route is chosen from the delta by the repository's rule - engine code is l7r/**/*.py and pool/*.gen.py|*.json - and none of the amendment paths are engine code. The enumeration on the line is incomplete as prose; the decision it records is unchanged and correct.

decisions.summary: The Constitution Check's XVI line reads 'no exception at the first landing; Amendment 2's P10 carries the GM's one exception, spec-fidelity, named in the tier test'.
decisions.why: It decides nothing; it restates the feature's own history, and both halves are true - the spec's Status line records the field set in all twelve at the first landing, and FR-013 excepts spec-fidelity alone thereafter with the tier test naming it. 'The GM's one exception' attributes the carve-out to the GM's authority, which their 'go with your recommendations to all three' did give; it does not claim they ruled it unprompted. Noted as an aside that this third line was not swept with P2's and P10's and could say 'the one exception the GM approved on the session's recommendation' for consistency.

decisions.summary: One test in the tier-test module, test_every_agent_launches_without_the_claude_md_files, requiring the field of every file in the already-derived roster, its message naming the field, the GM's ruling of 2026-09-19 and this feature; the module docstring gains that ruling; the tier table untouched.
decisions.why: FR-007 word for word as it then read, and the corrected wording DATES the ruling it rests on, which is the real one: request.md's first block, GM 2026-09-19, 'If there's something that a subagent should know, it should be in the subagent specification'. Verified in the shipped test: the assertion message carries 'feature 256, GM 2026-09-19' and the module docstring carries 'WHAT A DEFINED AGENT IS NOT HANDED (GM 2026-09-19, feature 256)'. FR-013 later narrows the guard's scope by one named agent and P10 records that change.

decisions.summary: The guard is proven by removing the field from one file and watching the test go red, and root CLAUDE.md's gate row for the tier test gains a clause naming what it now enforces.
decisions.why: The red proof is FR-007's second sentence verbatim (tasks T07 records it fired on entry-drift). The gate row is a one-clause documentation edit to a row that already exists for that file, and it now reads 'omitClaudeMd on every agent file but the one the test names'.

decisions.summary: spec-fidelity.md question 4's 'extra verification the GM did not request' becomes 'verification of something the GM did not ask for', with a paragraph after question 5 stating the distinction on this feature's round 1 as the worked example; spec-fidelity-verify.md gains the same paragraph.
decisions.why: FR-008 asks that BOTH fidelity contracts carry the GM's distinction and identifies question 4's phrase as the sentence that caused the cut. The authority is request.md's second block in the GM's own words.

decisions.summary: The fidelity-contract change is proven by ONE seeded run on round 1's own recorded prompt, scored on four items, with no control leg and no second case.
decisions.why: FR-008's own sentence and the repository's stated method for improving a review agent. Amendment 2 does not reopen the method: FR-012 rules on the RESULT of this run, not on its shape.

decisions.summary: make scatter-bases MAP=<pool map> in the skill Makefile (GUARD_EDIT_OK, a read-only diagnostic) with settlement-review's paragraph naming the target; the three (Tools: ...) tails cut; the seven contracts citing the tier test cite its real path.
decisions.why: FR-009 asks precisely for 'a make target wraps it and the contract names the target' plus the two cosmetic fixes the GM listed in request.md's second block. The plan leaves HOW the recipe reaches parse_bases open; the shipped work routes it through scripts/_scatter_bases.py with its own tests, still inside FR-009.

decisions.summary: The six agents with recorded runs are paired on named recorded cases, each cut to a slice the record already scored.
decisions.why: FR-010 asks for exactly these six, 'each on one recorded case with known findings'. spec-fidelity's pair is what produced the evidence Amendment 2's second decision rests on.

decisions.summary: building-review on tests/fixtures/ochiba-no-scale-red.svg and size-audit on tests/fixtures/ochiba-big-bath-red.svg, each staged in a HEAD worktree beside a copy of the Ochiba notes and rendered to PNG.
decisions.why: FR-010 asks for exactly this, scored against the CONTROL first by FR-003's rule; both defects are known by construction and both legs carry identical staging.

decisions.summary: All eight pairs run by FR-003's harness and rule with FR-004 governing a miss; sixteen runs, the batch's size stated before launch; settlement-review and perf-audit priced in research.md with their reasons.
decisions.why: FR-010's own words. The pricing reached the GM as the third of the three questions in request.md's third block, which is what 'put to the GM ... not decided by the session' asked for.

decisions.summary: T07 -> T08 -> T09 -> T10 -> T11 for Amendment 1.
decisions.why: It follows FR-007 to FR-011 in order; tasks.md T07-T11 name the same work with the same requirement ids.

decisions.summary: Amendment 2's section is headed 'P10 the GM's approval of three recommendations (FR-012 to FR-014)' and its guard sentence reads 'the hole in FR-007's guard is exactly the size of what the GM approved'.
decisions.why: This is the corrected wording under review, and it now states the authority accurately. request.md's third block is a session recommendation on each of three decisions and a GM answer of 'go with your recommendations to all three' - an approval, not an independent GM ruling, and the heading and the guard sentence say so. It matches the shipped record: KEEPS_CLAUDE_MD's value opens 'Approved by the GM on the session's recommendation, 2026-09-20 (they answered ... they did not raise the question)', root CLAUDE.md says 'which the GM approved on the session's measured recommendation, 2026-09-20', and spec FR-012 to FR-014 read the same way.

decisions.summary: No new machinery for Amendment 2; P7's paragraph in both fidelity contracts gains the test-versus-guard sentence in place.
decisions.why: FR-012 asks for exactly this, in the same change and in both contracts: a test that only FAILS when the requested thing is absent is verification; a guard that REFUSES, BLOCKS or REWRITES is behavior. It is the second half of the session's first recommendation, which the GM approved in their own words.

decisions.summary: omitClaudeMd is deleted from spec-fidelity.md alone, so eleven of the twelve defined agents launch without the CLAUDE.md files and the memory index instead of all twelve.
decisions.why: It narrows the GM's 2026-09-19 ruling that a DEFINED subagent should not be handed those files, and narrows FR-007's guard, so it is adjudicated rather than waved through. It survives because the carve-out is in the GM's own words in request.md's third block, not completed on their behalf: the session put the choice and the measurement ('I can keep the field on or take it off for this one agent. It gates every spec, its saving is small ... I recommend taking it off until a three-samples-per-leg test ... can tell field from variance') and the GM answered 'go with your recommendations to all three'. The carve-out's size is exactly what was approved - one named agent, not a class and not a criterion another agent could later meet - and it is time-bounded in FR-013 and in research R8 by the run that ends it. Verified in the tree: spec-fidelity.md is the only agent file without the field. The purpose of the GM's rule (a check is told what it needs in its own contract, not handed a session's files) is not gutted: FR-001's reading was done for spec-fidelity too, and its contract carries the rules it leans on either way.

decisions.summary: The tier test gains KEEPS_CLAUDE_MD, a name-to-reason table the guard skips and asserts is not stale, so the hole in FR-007's guard is the size of what the GM approved and cannot silently grow.
decisions.why: FR-013 settles the mechanism by name, and it enforces the approved scope rather than adding behavior of its own. Verified against the shipped test: KEEPS_CLAUDE_MD holds one row, spec-fidelity; wrong skips only names in that table; stale fails on a named agent that is gone or that carries the field after all. The table's comment now says an entry is 'a MEASURED case the GM approved, never a session's convenience ... Nothing goes in here on a session's own authority', which is the corrected authority statement in its strongest form.

decisions.summary: Root CLAUDE.md, the guard table's gate row, docs/efficiency-tooling.md and research.md R8 record the exception and what would end it.
decisions.why: These are the records FR-006 and P5 already own, kept true after the field's reach changed, plus SC-010's requirement that research.md says what would put the field back. Verified: each now describes the exception as the GM's approval of the session's measured recommendation. No document outside those the spec names is touched.

decisions.summary: settlement-review and perf-audit get no seeded pair and no harness at all; FR-014's watching of their first real dispatches stands in, with FR-004 as the route for what watching finds.
decisions.why: The GM's second block asked 'Is there any particular reason not to test the other 10 reviewers with seeded proofs?', so leaving two of the ten untested narrows the plain reading of that question and is adjudicated. It survives because the GM got the particular reason for each, priced, as the third of the three items in request.md's third block ('a single pair costs about 9 weight units and cannot separate a miss from variance ... perf-audit has nothing to replay ... roughly a day of session work. My recommendation is to skip both for now and watch their first real dispatches, but it is your call') and answered 'go with your recommendations to all three'. That is the GM answering their own question, not a session deciding it, and the two reasons are of the same class - no artifact to replay against - so one justification is not stretched over two unlike things.
T12 is the gate-and-land task the first landing also carried as T06; tasks.md T12 names the same work.
